Jay mentions Tidal’s numbers scandal to then point out the “Billboard hits” culture of Hip-Hop today. Industry artists often boast about their album sales and Billboard hits, including a young Jay. Even without these sales, Jay debuted the album at number one for the 13th time in a row. line: Three-fifths of a man, I believe’s the phrase
vault_lines: Three-fifths of a man, I believe's the phrase
meaning:
This is a reference to the 3/5th’s compromise of the US Constitution, proposed by James Wilson and Roger Sherman at the Constitutional Convention in 1787. While counting American censuses prior to the end of slavery, each slave was counted as 3/5 of a person. In other words, for every five slaves, three people were counted in the population.

This satisfied the larger, southern states, who could use large slave population to boost national representation, while not having to pay as much in taxes (issues proportionally to the population). At the same time, it somewhat appeased opponents of slavery in the Northern states, who believed that slaves should not be counted.

This compromise, which had major benefits for state power, was at the expense of African-Americans. It dehumanized African-Americans (remember, most blacks in the United States were slaves) and set the tone for their legal disenfranchisement for nearly 2 centuries.

This continues JAY-Z’s statement of irony in the previous line: America may be the land of the free, but since its inception, African-Americans have been treated differently based on the color of their skin.

“Four quarters” is “change,” but it’s also a reference to the way in which Meek has created his own persona and situation through the money he has made himself. It is indicative of how he views his career right now, and a nod to the plethora of “quarter” shout-outs in his music.

We can think that The Game is insinuating that this is because they are black, referencing the constant discrimination African-Americans have been the victim of for decades in the U.S.

PnB Rock (Rakim Hasheem Allen) died after being shot multiple times during a robbery at Roscoe’s Chicken & Waffles in Los Angeles on September 12, 2022. He was dining with his girlfriend when a gunman demanded his jewelry and then shot him before fleeing the scene.

meaning:
In this lyric, Meek is most likely describing a situation that many people go through in prisons across the country, hence the “bunk bed” analogy. If you ever end up in prison, arguably one of the last people you want to have beef with is your cellmate(s). Nighttime lockdowns in most prisons last anywhere from 10 P.M. to 6 A.M., meaning you’re locked in that cell for the next eight or so hours; if the people you’re sharing a cell with have problems with you, that can easily spell disaster.

Through this, Meek outlines a terrifying situation where he could barely get any sleep at night due to fear of being harmed or killed by his own cellmate. That, mixed with the every day drama that can occur in a cellblock, can create a scary situation for both the person incarcerated and their loved ones.

The selling of homemade soul food or “dinner platters” is a common “hustle” around holidays in inner city Philadelphia, and similar urban locations. Since many matriarchs will already be making large meals to feed their family and holiday guests, many make extra food to sell to friends and neighbors.

Dinner platters usually consist of a fried protein, such as chicken or fish, collard greens and baked macaroni and cheese.

This line relates to the last bar where Meek mentions Easter Weekend, a time when many people would be making and selling soul food dinner platters.

ladder is common slang term for an extended ammunition magazine or “clip.”



In this instance, Meek is using the word to refer to the gun in general and/or the ammunition contained in the clip. Since an extended clip holds more bullets than a standard clip, the holder(s) are able to get off more shots at once without the need to reload and are more likely to be able to deliver a shot that will kill the target.

Meek is saying that at the time the boy was being shot to death, the boy’s mother was in the kitchen making food to sell on Easter Weekend.

meaning:
Cutting a deck refers to the procedure where the dealer completes the shuffle, and then sets the cards face-down on the table near the designated player, typically the player to the dealer’s right. The player cuts the deck by removing a contiguous range of cards from the deck, and places them toward himself so that the stack of cards to be dealt is closest to the dealer.

In this case, Meek’s the dealer, and he’s not dealing cards.. he’s dealing coke. Cutting a brick of cocaine refers to diluting the drug to increase its weight and maximize profit.

Also, note the wordplay on shuffle and cut it, since Meek is clearly not in the dope game anymore. He’s “cutting” songs, and a popular option for any playback device is the “shuffle” option. Playing off of the long running trope of comparing making music to making dope, like Kanye previously said in his song “Crack Music”.

line: OG is one who standin’ on his own feet
vault_lines: OG is one who standin' on his own feet
meaning:
The term O.G. is the acronym for Original Gangster with the roots dating back to 1972 when Original was used by the Crips. It was used to insinuate that “we’re first”, the Originals. Two years later the word “Gangster” was added to form the Original Gangster Crips and they only used the term “O.G.” when writing their name or their neighbourhood.

Since then, the term O.G. has been widely used in hip-hop and hood culture in reference to original individuals within a certain area or just someone successful or highly skilled in any given area.

Rick Ross shares more of his wisdom with us in his verse on Ima Boss where he mentions how an O.G. is someone who can take care of themselves, who can achieve success in a certain field. Whereas a boss (pronounced “bawse” by Rick Ross) is someone who guarantees all their boys eat.

To expand this further, the term eat is used to describe success in such a way that everyone reaps and benefits from it. The prime example of this as always is a figure such as Jay-Z, who throughout the years has guaranteed quite a few people gon’ eat.

To quote him on this from his verse on “Pound Cake”:

I’ve done made more millionaires than the lotto did
Dame made millions, Biggs made millions
Ye made millions, Just made millions
Lyor made millions, Cam made millions
Beans’a tell you if he wasn’t in his feelings

Meek starts the album title track by addressing the youth; Young'uns/young'ins is a slang term for a person who is young.

Here is the definition of a First Down in American Football (for those not familiar with American Football lingo):

Each team has four downs to move the ball 10 yards. If it is able to do that, the team is awarded a new set of downs. First down is the first of those four attempts. When a team is able to move the ball upfield by 10 or more yards, it is awarded a new set of downs–that is referred to as “gaining a first down”, as the team now starts playing a first down again having four chances to move the ball 10 yards.

line: ’Member they told me that we would fail ’Member they said we would see a cell
vault_lines: 'Member they told me that we would fail
meaning:
In these lines, Meek Mill is recalling the doubt and negativity that people had toward him and his circle in the past. When he says “’Member they told me that we would fail,” he is referring to how others predicted that he would not succeed in life or in his career.

The next line, “’Member they said we would see a cell,” refers to the expectation that he and people around him would end up in prison (“a cell”). This reflects his background, where incarceration and street life were common outcomes that others assumed were inevitable.

Overall, these lines emphasize overcoming adversity. Meek Mill is highlighting how people underestimated him, expecting failure or prison, but he managed to rise above those predictions and achieve success instead.

line: To light up the city like Meechie in ’03
vault_lines: To light up the city like Meechie in '03
meaning:
In this line, Meek Mill is comparing his ambition and impact to “Meechie in ’03,” referring to Demetrius “Big Meech” Flenory, the co-founder of the Black Mafia Family (BMF), a powerful drug trafficking organization in the United States during the early 2000s.

At that time, Big Meech was known for being extremely influential, wealthy, and highly visible, especially in urban culture and hip-hop circles. The year 2003 represents the peak of BMF’s power and lifestyle, marked by luxury, attention, and dominance in the streets.

So when Meek Mill says “To light up the city like Meechie in ’03,” he is expressing his desire to have a similar level of presence and influence. He wants to stand out, dominate his environment, and be widely recognized, just like Big Meech was at his peak.

line: Was it the money that made me a savage?
vault_lines: Was it the money that made me a savage?
meaning:
In this line, Meek Mill is reflecting on how money and success may have changed him as a person. When he says “Was it the money that made me a savage?”, he is questioning whether becoming wealthy made him more aggressive, cold, or ruthless.

Coming from a difficult background, he had to develop a tough mentality to survive. However, after gaining fame and financial success, he starts to wonder if the money intensified that mindset or altered his personality in a negative way. The word “savage” here suggests someone who is hardened, less emotional, and more willing to do whatever it takes.

Overall, the line shows self-awareness and doubt. He is not just celebrating success, but also reflecting on its consequences, questioning whether money made him lose part of his humanity or simply reinforced the toughness he already had.

In these lines from Owl Pharaoh, Travis Scott is addressing jealousy and potential threats from others who resent his success.


“All these niggas hatin' on me, know they wanna body me (Bands)”
He’s saying that people who dislike him—likely due to his rising fame and wealth—harbor violent intentions (“wanna body me” means they want to kill or harm him). The mention of “Bands” (money) suggests that their envy is fueled by his financial success.
“‘Cause every time you see a nigga, I look like a robbery”
Here, he’s implying that his appearance—likely dressed in expensive clothes, jewelry, and flashing wealth—makes him look like someone who just committed a robbery, meaning he’s carrying a lot of money or valuables. This line plays on the idea that his wealth is so apparent that it could make him a target.
“Blow”
This could be an ad-lib or a reference to gun violence, signaling potential retaliation or the dangers that come with his success.



Overall, this verse reflects the paranoia and reality of fame, where wealth attracts both admiration and danger. It ties into hip-hop themes of success, envy, and the risks that come with being in the spotlight.

The word  Bands  is slang for large amounts of money, often referring to stacks of cash held together by rubber bands. This reinforces the idea that financial motives are at play in the relationship he’s describing.

Overall, the line reflects themes of materialism, superficial relationships, and honesty, which are common in Travis Scott’s early music.

This line is similar to one Jay Z spat on his “All The Way Up Remix”:

I’m on the penthouse floor, call your way up

Mobile phones will work when airborne, but only within the range of cellular towers. Kiss' career is at such a high altitude no reception is possible.

vault_lines: Opps in the building, automatically alert that

“Opps” are any form of opposition, usually cops but possibly rival dealers. His radar is finely tuned to identify trouble, and on this occasion he’s identified multiple threats.

In order to eliminate them, he’ll have to shoot more than once, or “squirt.” However, he’s aware that the recoil from large handgun he’s carrying may impair his aim, so he places his supporting hand on his main wrist when shooting to minimise the jerk back, increasing accuracy.

vault_lines: J all I know is 500, getchu a thousand

Moving through the hood unabated showcases his OG status, and as he said on “Somehow, Someway (Freestyle)”:

Yall scared of yall hood but I love mine

line: Nah, I’m built for the physical outing Besides that, I’m filthy, like municipal housing
vault_lines: Nah, I'm built for the physical outing
meaning:
Jada refers to throwing hands, or fist fighting. He’s accused other rappers previously of their lack of physical presence, on “All Falls Down”:

Niggas' pants too tight to fight, so they don’t want it

Municipal housing is the public housing system in the US, designed to provide a home for those less fortunate. Kiss plays on a stereotype that, because it’s not legally “their” house, they are less clean than usual.

line: And you know my boys hold it, we be out with the ratchets I heard your boys told her you be out with the rats Keep that on the ”Shhhh!”, nothing less, nothing more
vault_lines: And you know my boys hold it, we be out with the ratchets
meaning:
Fab’s moved on from keeping a weapon on him, as detailed on 2009’s “Imma Do It”:

That’s why I’m with naudia I call my gun naudia
When she say hi to ya it’s buh buh bye to ya

He even uses a similar double meaning here. Ratchet is both a gun and a girl from the hood who acts like a diva. Another bad actress.

A “rat” is a police informant, and Fab warns this person that the guns held by his crew won’t be quiet for long if he continues this behaviour.

line: I just played the cards they dealt me ’til a change-up was due Guess I had to switch the dealer or just change up the shoe Now blackjack, Ace of Spade and a shot of Jack
vault_lines: I just played the cards they dealt me 'til a change-up was due
meaning:
“Switching the dealer” and “changing up the shoe” are both actions related to card playing, especially the game of blackjack.  In the context of the game, a card player may exercise these rights to, essentially, turn his or her luck by starting off fresh.  One might make these changes when one can no longer suffice with “the cards with which they were dealt.”

“Ace” and “Jack” refer to two different types of cards and two different alcoholic drinks—Ace of Spades champagne and Jack Daniel’s whiskey.

Fabolous uses this metaphor to depict the adjustments he needed to make to reach his current level of success.



His “dealer switch” could be his move to Roc Nation in 2014.

line: Should get out your feelings bro, and get in your duffle, boy
vault_lines: Should get out your feelings bro, and get in your duffle, boy
meaning: Despite Fab showing a dislike for subliminals, this feels like a subliminal shot. Being “in your feelings” is to act or speak purely on emotion, not logic or with rational thought. A duffle bag is commonly used in the hood to carry guns or money, so Fab urges this person to stop acting emotional and make money or facilitate violence.

line: I’m kicking you off the ladder for trying to climb up Yup, overlooking the city
vault_lines: I'm all the way up
meaning:
This is a subliminal reference to Drake’s Views album art.

It seems as though Kiss is removing Drake from the “greatest rapper of all time conversation” due to the ghostwriter allegations. During an Uncommon Sense episode, Kiss said:

There’s no way you should be able. It should be a headline.

He also alluded to the fact that anyone with a ghostwriter can not be considered as a top rapper.

line: She jumped in the 6, 550 wasn’t big enough
vault_lines: She jumped in the 6, 550 wasn't big enough
meaning:
Jada mentions the Mercedes Maybach S600, a $200,000 car which features a cavernous interior.



His girl prefers this over the standard S550, which only costs around $100k and is a full 8 inches shorter.

line: Reason niggas die, they don’t know how to live enough They can tread water, but they can’t swim enough
vault_lines: Reason niggas die, they don't know how to live enough
meaning:
This relates to both rappers, and street personalities. During “Incarcerated Scarfaces,” Jada took aim at bangers who don’t know how to move correctly to keep themselves alive and out of prison:

Shallow minds usually drown in deep waters

Rappers must learn to swim as well, and Kiss likened the game to an ocean in “Welcome to the Roc”:

I’m well determined, dedicated with devotion
Never a smooth sail, it’s rough water in the Oceans
Higher in the ranks, I’m hotter than you think

One hit wonders die out because they’re not built for the intensity of the game. Jada has been successful for 18 years, so he knows a thing or two about swimming.

line: I’m all the way up, I’m like Hov looking at Biggie
vault_lines: I'm all the way up, I'm like Hov looking at Biggie
meaning: Although Jay had known The Notorious B.I.G. since high school, their first real meeting was in 1995 during the recording of “Brooklyn’s Finest.” Jay looked up to Big, and has constantly paid homage. When Jay was releasing his first record, B.I.G. was already platinum, and one of the most successful rappers not only in the city, but the country.

line: Level up, level up, it’s all about that level up Hold that fuckin’ bezel up and light this bitch all the way up
vault_lines: I'm all the way up
meaning: A bezel is the frame of a watch. Fab’s bezel has so many diamonds in that it’s bright enough to light up the whole room.

line: Talkin’ loud, say I’m shootin’ out with metal objects
vault_lines: Talkin' loud, say I'm shootin' out with metal objects
meaning:
Meek’s earlier basketball reference takes on further significance, after he took shots at Drake’s middle class upbringing.  During Degrassi High Drake was a school basketball star. Meek was a star too, except he was shooting guns not balls.

Numerous news sources have accused Meek of yelling during his raps, and he explains it’s simply because he’s used to the sound of guns exploding.

line: Bout to go and grab the Benz truck, see y’all later When I came through the block, you should’ve seen y’all faces
vault_lines: Bout to go and grab the Benz truck, see y'all later
meaning:
Buying new, expensive cars is a daily expenditure for Meek. This time around, he’s about to cop a Mercedes G-class.

These trucks have a starting price of about $120,000, and are driven by a multitude of celebrities, including the Kardashians.

line: What’s up with your Warriors? They ain’t lookin’ tough no more
vault_lines: What's up with your Warriors? They ain't lookin' tough no more
meaning:
The opposing crew’s “warriors” are shook. He may be referring to the 1979 film The Warriors, a  movie about a street gang that has to fight their way through New York, or the NBA’s Golden State Warriors, who were down 3-1 in a best of 7 series against the Oklahoma City Thunder at the time this song was released. Those Warriors had broken record for wins in a regular season, but hadn’t looked like their dominant selves at that point in the series. The Warriors eventually went on to come back and win the series against the Thunder.

Fab is famous for his sporting references, particularly Basketball.

line: Meek called me and Fab, Joe called Jigga up
vault_lines: Meek called me and Fab, Joe called Jigga up
meaning:
While Meek called up Jada and Fab for his remix of “All The Way Up,” Fat Joe called up Jay Z (via Memphis Bleek) for their remix.



Note that everyone on Jay’s remix is from New York. This was intentional, as Fat Joe said:

I turned down some really really really big names for the remix. Like, the biggest guys on Earth but was just like, yo, I wanna keep it New York.

Jadakiss is also from New York, but it’s possible Meek called him first for this remix. Kiss and Meek have been tight ever since 2013’s “Heaven or Hell,” and Meek has claimed Jadakiss was like a “second father” to him just from his music.

line: I know the Bad Boys in Brooklyn, they ain’t with the Puffy tour
vault_lines: I know the Bad Boys in Brooklyn, they ain't with the Puffy tour
meaning:
A reference to the Bad Boy Reunion tour, which Puff Daddy (a.k.a Diddy) hosted in Brooklyn, New York City, in May 2016.

While Fab knows Puffy’s on tour, he doesn’t just know those Bad Boys—he knows the real “bad boys” (gang bangers) in the streets of his home town, as he explained on “Brooklyn”:

Bed-Stuy fly, Bushwick sick
East New York walk the Brownsville grill, ill
You see, I got a Fort Greene lean
Clinton Hill chill, Red Hook look, man

A nic is a $5 bag of drugs (weed, crack, dope, etc) and is a popular way of selling drugs on the streets of Philly.



Unlike Drake, Meek has experienced the street life and most likely has seen $50,000 in $5 notes.

line: Mixin’ D’usse with lemonade when I’m in Georgia
vault_lines: Mixin' D'usse with lemonade when I'm in Georgia
meaning:
This is a reference to hip-hop’s most powerful couple, Jay Z and Beyoncé, along with Mr. Rugs, D'usse brand ambassador and friend of Fabulous. Jay and Rugs are well known for marketing the Cognac D'usse Liquor—Jay in his raps and Rugs in Georgia, and Beyoncé has accumulated extensive buzz and gossip with her sixth studio album, LEMONADE. Jay acknowledged the album on his “All The Way Up (Remix)”:

Lemonade is a popular drink and it still is
Survival of the littest

The mixing of these two drinks signify that their relationship must be strong. Meek has said in the past his relationship with Nicki Minaj is inspired by the iconic couple.

line: Catch you out in traffic, it’s you and I Gold 41 in a suit and tie, nigga it’s do or die Seen it now, if I lose it all like who would ride?
vault_lines: Catch you out in traffic, it's you and I
meaning:
Most of Meek’s verse is addressed to Drake, the pair have been beefing since July 2015 when Meek accused Drake of not writing his own raps. While it seems Meek’s prepared to stake his career on winning the battle with Drake, he still wonders if he loses, will there be anyone left by his side?

“Catch you out in traffic” implies a drive by shooting, while a Gold 41 refers to a 41mm face on a watch.

line: But I’m shootin’ like the Warriors’ startin’ 5, swish!
vault_lines: But I'm shootin' like the Warriors' startin' 5, swish!
meaning:
Even though Meek lives dangerous on the streets, he still comes out as a winner. Just like the Warriors' starting 5, he takes the shot (risk) but he mostly scores (succeeds).



The Golden State Warriors lineup, also know as the “Lineup of death,” consists of Stephen Curry, Klay Thompson, Andre Iguodala, Harrison Barnes and Draymond Green. It is viewed as one of the most difficult lineups for opposing teams to deal with, averaging a 77.8 True Shooting Percentage.

line: Ain’t about throwin’ subs, I’m about gettin’ scratches But if the shoe fits, nigga, buy an outfit to match it
vault_lines: Ain't about throwin' subs, I'm about gettin' scratches
meaning:
“Subs” is a shortened version of the phrase “subliminal messages,” a way to throw shots without explicitly mentioning a rappers name. Fab is adept at these, throwing shade at Drake on his version of “Lord Knows”:

You gotta watch the picture that you painting with your verses
We go in niggas' mouths, I don’t know bout bitches' purses
And what’s up with this, “I’m just sayin'” shit?
Fuck asked you? You shouldn’t be saying shit

The lines were a reference to Drake’s “Marvin’s Room.” Drake is a master of the subliminal war, and Fab seems to dismiss that here, saying he’s willing to explicitly call rappers out and deal with the physical consequences. If you see something that offends you, good, that was his intention.

line: They don’t wanna see you on top I just wanna see the streets up They don’t wanna see you up That’s it They gon’ take shots when you all the way up
vault_lines: I'm all the way up
meaning:
The opening bars to Fab’s verse are a nod to DJ Khaled’s “They don’t want you to win” mantra, featured in many of his Snapchat videos.



“They” in relation to Fab is a small circle. He’s respected in the industry, and not known for high profile beefs. He did have words with Drake, after the Canadian dissed him an interview, but Fab deaded that in 2014.

It’s the classic “tall poppy syndrome.” Haters will try to cut you down when you’re at the very top of your game. Fab’s circle and crew is so tight, beef’s rarely see the light of day.

line: If she for everybody, don’t you let her claim up on you

Fab’s advice: if a girl is known for hooking up and having sex with a lot of other men, don’t date her. It’ll make you look bad and other guys will be able to say they “hit that.”

Fab’s dating history is populated by more than one girl who fits this description, with both Karrine Steffans and Amber Rose rumoured to be past hook-ups. Although Fab has denied the Amber Rose link, many believe the hook up occurred.

http://imgur.com/jaryCPa

However, this may be a reference to Quentin Miller, who was accused of ghostwriting both Meek and Drake. Starting with “unHOLY,” Quentin managed to deny the allegations, but later confirmed his allegiance on “Going Back”:

I’m going back to the Six
Going back to the Six
Yeah
Yeah, I’m going back to the Six

Fab keeps his circle tight, and takes aim at those who pledge their allegiance but change, whether because of money, women, or jealousy.

This is a reprise of his classic track “Change Up,” off 2007’s From Nothin' To Somethin'“:

Some niggas change when they get change, funny when they get money
Switch when they get rich, strayed when they got paid

During Drake’s “Hype”  from Views he raps:

Don’t you see RiRi right next to me?

Rumours that Meek and Rihanna had hooked up began to surface in 2013, although Meek denied these.

Is this a confirmation that something happened? There were claims Meek was beefing with Chris Brown over the alleged tryst, and fans speculated that his withering line on “I’m Da Plug (Freestyle)” was actually about Rihanna:

You took her to an island, I fucked her on a couch
I fucked her in the studio, she never seen my house
She told me that you’re lame, I told her clean you out
I got that pussy same day she made you eat her out, woo!

Drake’s relationship with her is long and storied. Did Meek get there first?

line: But nigga I’m so up, if I tripped it’s like suicide
vault_lines: But nigga I'm so up, if I tripped it's like suicide
meaning:
Meeks lyrical finesse is so advanced that he’d be hurting himself if he put out something or did something that wasn’t him.  He feels if he put out a song or album that wasn’t up to the world’s and his standards, his career would fall into shambles.

In another sense, Meek employs clever imagery that relies upon the listener to interpret the line physically.  Like a highwire walker (or any other person that is high up), a single mistake can be fatal.

line: She hang like a chain so she ’bout to get snatched
vault_lines: She hang like a chain so she 'bout to get snatched

The girl is hanging with the crew so Fab is about to take her.

If your chain is “hanging,” it’s easy for someone to steal. Many people will tuck their chains in their shirt when they are in unfamiliar cities.

line: I came back like I’m Mike wearin’ 45
vault_lines: I came back like I'm Mike wearin' 45
meaning:
After Michael Jordan retired from basketball (the first time), the Bulls retired his #23 jersey. When he returned he wore #45. Like Jordan, Meek has come back with a vengeance.



Also, this line pays homage to a similar Jay Z line from his song “Encore” from The Black Album.

When I come back like Jordan, wearing the 4-5
It ain’t to play games with you, it’s to aim at you, probably maim you
If I owe you I’m blowin' you to smithereens

line: Views from the projects, and nigga I’m the prospect
vault_lines: Views from the projects, and nigga I'm the prospect
meaning:
Meek makes a play on the original title of Drake’s fourth studio album, Views From The 6. Later the album was cut short to  simply Views.

Meek Mill is from the streets, so he really did start from the bottom. When a rapper starts to gain traction in their home town, people pin their hope on them making it out of the hood. Meek had to come up alongside Major Figgas, Freeway, Beanie Sigel and Cassidy, but at just 29 he’s younger than all of them, and putting the city on his back. He’s “Mr. Philadelphia.”

line: I was on the block when you was a sneakerhead Nigga it’s a check up in that box, ain’t no shoe inside Nigga ain’t no Nike, ain’t no Yeezy, no Jordan V
vault_lines: I was on the block when you was a sneakerhead
meaning:
On an episode of MTV Cribs, teenage Drake gives a tour of his home and shows off his sneaker collection. While Nike and Yeezy are both popular sneaker brands, Meek specifically mentions the Jordan 5’s, one of the most popular sneakers of all time.

https://youtu.be/7OisZAqxeEI?t=175

When Meek was this age, he was in the streets, counting money in his shoe boxes. Also, note the play on words—the Nike logo is as a “check” and “check” (as in a money) is inside the box.

line: I met a bad actress, she ain’t know how to act I took her but I brought her back Don’t want her back, I bought her bag Matte like Hasselbeck, I call my car a quarterback If I threw it at her would you doubt she could catch?
vault_lines: I met a bad actress, she ain't know how to act
meaning:
This is a sexual innuendo and reference to former NFL quarterback Matt Hasselbeck. Fab met up with an actress who has an attractive appearance and personality, but she’s from the hood, so she doesn’t know how to act around wealth, hence she’s a “bad actress.” He also copped her a matte handbag, a play on Matt Hasselbeck and maybe a reference to the $120k Hermes Matte Crocodile Skin bag.

The actress Fab is referring to could be one of his ex girlfriends. Amber Priddy, Tahiry Jose and Erica Mena are all small time actresses, appearing on shows like Love and Hip Hop New York.



Fab’s car is his penis. Even though he’s moved on from these girls, he speculates that if he offered them sex they’d say yes.

line: Only rapper went gold without a verse from Hov Still got the rock with me, cookin’ up at the stove
vault_lines: Only rapper went gold without a verse from Hov
meaning:
Meek’s right about going gold without a verse from Jay Z—his debut album Dreams & Nightmares is certified gold, and he’s never been blessed with a verse from HOV. However, he’s definitely not the only rapper to do this.

Kendrick Lamar went gold with good kid, m.A.A.d city before Jay Z jumped on the “Bitch Don’t Kill My Vibe” remix, and A$AP Rocky has gone gold with both Long. Live. A$AP and At. Long. Last. ASAP without a verse from Hov. Other rappers to go gold without a verse from Hov include Childish Gambino, Iggy Azalea, Wale, Kid Cudi, Kevin Gates, 2 Chainz, YG, G-Eazy, Future, Kid Ink, Big Sean, Bryson Tiller, Mac Miller, Macklemore, Wiz Khalifa, and Nicki Minaj. Drake, on the other hand, has listed a HOV writing credit on 3 of his 4 studio albums.

It’s also worth noting the play on words with Roc (Roc-A-Fella) and rock (crack).

line: I give ’em the dirty flow, Michigan and water Sent them 10 thousand cases, I put in my order Call that poppin’ bottles when my people can’t afford it
vault_lines: I give 'em the dirty flow, Michigan and water
meaning:
Meek Mill is referring to the water crisis in Flint, Michigan. The water in Flint contained extremely unhealthy and dirty water, unfit for human consumption. Many rappers have showed support to the people of Flint and their struggle.

Meek challenged 50 Cent to donate $50,000 to Flint during the height of their water crisis. Meek donated, 50 did not. Instead, 50 continued to pop bottles in the club while people in Flint suffered.

line: I was Kyrie with the rock, the crack game number 2 Now I’m older, still ballin’ like my name Uncle Drew
vault_lines: I was Kyrie with the rock, the crack game number 2
meaning:
Fab references basketball player Kyrie Irving, who wears number 2 and is known to be an excellent ball-handler. ‘The Rock’ in this bar has a double meaning. In basketball the rock is the ball, and in the drug dealing game, the rock is cocaine in rock form aka crack.

When he mentions the “crack game number 2,” he’s saying he’s the Kyrie Irving of drug dealing.
Fab is 38 now, so he references Uncle Drew, an elder ball player character that Kyrie plays in Sprite commercials, to show he’s still at the top of his game despite his age.

line: When the internet told me I’m crucified They was in them streets like, “Nigga you super live”
vault_lines: When the internet told me I'm crucified
meaning:
While the internet was making memes and clowning Meek after Drake dropped consecutive diss tracks “Charged Up” and “Back To Back,” the streets had his back.

Drake also projected a slideshow of memes during his performance of “Back To Back” at the 2015 OVO Fest in Toronto.

In an interview with Noisey, Pusha T used the exact same words as Meek:

I just feel like the principles of 2002 aren’t the principles of 2015. You know? I listen to both, I listen to both Meek music, I listen to Drake music, both, you know. I don’t know, I just watched how people handled it, and I watched how the media handled it, and I just have to say that—you don’t crucify people who didn’t lie to you. And I sort of feel like people tried to crucify Meek, but he didn’t lie. You crucify people that lie to you; you don’t crucify the person that doesn’t lie to you, so. I think that is an example of where people are in the world, who the critics are, and so on and so forth.

line: Made me beat a fan up, I’m feelin’ like I’m Artest, woo!
vault_lines: Made me beat a fan up, I'm feelin' like I'm Artest, woo!
meaning:
During a Meek concert in September 2015 in New York, a Drake fan turned up with a sign supporting the Toronto MC. Meek responded with this:

Put that Drake sign up again, n***a. Fuck you talkin’ ’bout you fuckin’ clown. Don’t ever come in here and fuckin’ play on no Meek Mill, tryna pick on me like I’m a fuckin’ dweeb or somethin’.

He’s comparing this situation to the infamous Pacers vs Pistons fight, known as “Malice at the Palace,” in which player Ron Artest sparked a huge brawl between players and fans when he was hit by a drink thrown by a spectator.

line: Got the hood super lit, jumpin’ like it’s double dutch From the bottom like an uppercut, now I’m all the way up
vault_lines: I'm all the way up, I'm like Hov looking at Biggie
meaning:
Drake’s “Started From the Bottom,” Meek claims, applies much more to him than his Toronto rival. “Lit” means excited, turnt up, and “double dutch” is a complicated jump rope game. Meek’s the prospect after all.



An uppercut begins low and ends high, which traces a similar arc to Meek’s career.

line: Now listen, you gave up on me, I came up on you Took my talents somewhere else, LeBron James up on you
vault_lines: Now listen, you gave up on me, I came up on you

This is a reference to when LeBron James announced he would be taking his talents to South Beach to join the Heat in a interview with ESPN “The Decision”:

In this fall, this is very tough, in this fall I’m going to take my talents to South Beach and join the Miami Heat.



It’s also a nod to Fab’s own line on DJ Drama’s “Oh My”:

I got one in Miami, she mean with a mouth piece, like LeBron I’m taking my talents down to south beach

Fab may be opening an old wound. There were claims he was unhappy during his deal with Atlantic Records, and felt the promotion of album Real Talk was lacklustre. He signed to Def Jam, and is now managed by Roc Nation. He took his talents elsewhere.

line: And the Rollie all platinum, know I bust it at Joe Maybach in the hood, so them suckers can know
vault_lines: And the Rollie all platinum, know I bust it at Joe

Meek is well known for dropping references to his platinum Rolex and Maybach in his raps. Joe is Meek’s personal jeweler, owner of Shyne Jewelers in Philly. “Bust it” means adding diamonds to the bezel.

“Maybach in the hood, so them suckers can now” refers to Meeks 90 days under house arrest. Although he’s supposed to stay inside, the neighbourhood knows he’s out because they see a  Mercedes-Maybach S600—Meek’s the only person in the neighbourhood that owns one.

line: This is slaughter, new world order I be goin’ hard, Westbrook, 4th quarter
vault_lines: This is slaughter, new world order

Meek suggests that anyone who has beef with him will be destroyed and that he sets up a New World Order, or totalitarian system in which he rules over the world.



Russel Westbrook is the point guard for the Oklahoma City Thunder. Meek is going hard in his raps, as a basketball player would in the 4th quarter of the game. Meek has improve leaps and bounds since his first diss track, “Wanna Know.”

line: Gold mic from the billboards, ’bout to plug it up Tell Cruz put it in the booth so I can fuck it up
vault_lines: Gold mic from the billboards, 'bout to plug it up

On the 23rd of May, 2016 Meek took home the Billboard Music Award for Best Rap Album, beating two Drake records in the process.



Anthony Cruz is a popular Sound Engineer who Meek works with. Meek wants his award in the booth so he can prove that he earned the title.

He also again references his “I’m Da Plug (Freestyle)” diss track that dropped in early 2016.

line: I’m in the 6, man, 6 man, Dion Waiters And I’m on my level now, I’m so beyond haters

Dion Waiters is a professional NBA player who played for Oklahoma City Thunder. Dion and Meek are both from Philly. In 2012, Dion worked to accomplish the Sixth Man of The Year, as Meek did for the gold mic.

Meek mentions Waiters in Rick Ross' “So Sophisticated”:

Shitting on these haters, ball hard D Waiters
Ever since I got money, e’rybody need favors

This may also be another jab at Drake, who released a song titled “6 Man” on his 2015 mixtape If You’re Reading This It’s Too Late. Meek feels as if he’s starting to rise above Drake.

line: This is hip-hop, you ain’t write it, don’t record it I don’t know how they gettin’ down ’cross the border

This is a direct reference to Drake, who’s Canadian, hence “across the border.” Meek and Drizzy have been involved in a feud since July 2015 when Meek accused Drake of not writing his own raps.

Traditionally, hip-hop is a genre that expects artists to be real and honest with their work. Drake received help from Quentin in the past to make some of his greatest hits, but didn’t give much recognition for his talent.

I just wanna know, if you ain’t write that running through the six shit

According to Chris’s hook, Meek and Nicki met at the club and decided right then and there to become a couple. Given what we know about their history, it’s more likely that the hook isn’t strictly based on reality.

In December 2014, Nicki shot down any rumor that she was dating Meek Mill, making it clear that she was “not on the market” but planned to work with Meek on her album The Pinkprint. On The Pinkprint, Meek and Nicki hinted at romance on “Buy A Heart,” and their relationship seemed to escalate in the following months, with Nicki confirming that they were “hanging out” in February 2015.
